notes.title: Version 1.4 Update: New game modes and new price
notes.notes:
It's already been 6 months and time flies.

Version 1.4 is the update in charge of celebrate this milestone with 2 significant changes.

The first one is GAME MODES:

Now, first and foremost game modes will not change the puzzle mechanic of the game or the overall gameplay of Hoping Forest. Game modes change the speed and pace of the game for those who are looking for a more quick and expedited experience for the game.

The first game mode is Fast Paced: In this mode, the frog movement, camera transitions, and score screen animations are up to twice as fast. This option is aimed at those who would like a bit faster transition between levels but don't want to miss anything. The speed will still let you appreciate the path you create and will show you your result and score, but will reduce significantly in the long run the time needed to complete the game.

The second one is Speed Run: This mode removes completely the score screen, causing instant transition or reset of levels in addition to up to three times faster camera transition and frog movement.
This option is aimed at those who just want to focus on solutions to the puzzles and don't care about anything else. You won't get feedback on your result and score and you might not be able to appreciate the path you create, but since completing levels is your main goal, it could not be a big loss for you. This mode also enables the Start run button on level selection. This option lets you start from level 1 of zone 1 without the need to finish the tutorial. If someone actually wants to try doing a speedrun of Hoping Forest this button could be what you are looking for.


The second big change is a price update:

First I would like to say a few things. Pricing a game is hard, is not easy to put a price tag on your work and effort, and that's not different when we are talking about indie games, specially on Steam.
Originally I thought 5 USD could be a fair price for the game, but ended up convincing myself to increasing it up to 9 USD after doing some research on similar games and adding more levels, at first the game consisted of 40 levels and I ended up developing 60. 
If I'm being honest I still believe 9 USD is not a bad price when contrasted with overall pricing of things (is around the same cost as a fast food meal or a movie ticket), but I agree it feels expensive for an indie game, and when compared to Steam prices of indie games even more. And the fact that is the first published game of a random solo indie developer doesn't help.
Almost every feedback and criticism of the game mentions the fact that the price felt a bit too much and with time I came to agree with that. And that's why I moving the price back to what I originally thought and setting it at 4.99$. I doubt I will change the price again in the future and will only rely on Steam sales and discounts. But who knows, in a few years that might change.

For now, I hope the new price convinces a few folks who had it on their wishlist to pick it up or just wait for the next Steam sale and grab it even cheaper. As long as people can enjoy my game I don't really care that much what they pay for it.


And that's all for now. I mentioned some time ago that there are a few things cooking in the back and that's still up, but it will take a bit more time, I hope I can share more before the end of the year.

SO... tldr: New game modes for those who are looking for a faster experience and a new price. Don't miss this chance to play Hoping Forest and enjoy this relaxing but challenging experience.

notes.title: General Update: Overhaul of some systems and Future Plans.
notes.notes:
🐸 - A new update for Hoping Forest is here! - 🐸

First and foremost thanks for all the support in these 2 weeks.

I doubt that I’ll update the game in a weekly schedule but at least in this update, I was able to add some of the things that were left out for the official launch.

First of all, there is a small overhaul on how the game shows progress. Previously you could only see it in the general view on the main menu, which could affect those players that were looking for the 100%, now each zone shows its progress in the level selection adding more clarity on what you are missing. 
On the same note, at the end of zone 4, there is a hidden level but there was no indicator of what that was, which could lead to thinking it was a bug or something. Now it has a small hint of what to do with it.

There is also a small improvement in the screen flow. Until now if you went back to the menu from the puzzles you were led to the main screen. Making it a bit tedious for those who were trying to complete the 100% or just wanted to change levels. Now the Back to Menu buttons led you to the level selection screen optimizing the access to different levels for those looking for the 100%.

The way the score count works in the tutorial was changed. Before the introduction of flies, the score in the tutorial levels was different from the rest of the game. This was on purpose as a way to show whether someone completed the tutorial on the first attempt or not. However, this led to weird interactions and could make players think it was a bug or something of the sort. 
Since the score of the tutorial is not taken into account for the 100% this was modified to work similar to how the rest of the game works. Now if you failed a tutorial level before the introduction of flies you don’t get medals and if you complete it you get all the medals.



There were also some small bugs fixed, especially those that affect the progression of the game, and the speed of some UI animations was tweaked.

Now, the other important part of this update, my plans for the future of the game.

Right now I’m happy with the state of the game. But I do know there are some areas where the game could be improved upon.

One of the is a speedrun mode

I’m evaluating different ways to add a game mode and/or options within the game that could allow a more fast and more dynamic experience, especially considering UI and animations.
I’m still thinking about this so there is no date for this yet or if it will be developed at all, so take everything with a grain of salt.
In any case, anything I’ll end up doing about this will be optional and an alternative to the recommended way to play the game. You might even need to finish the game before accessing this game mode.

The other thing I believe the game could be improved upon is the  addition of a story

Originally some sort of narrative was planned for the game, there is even a comic-style cinematic system working within the game but since this is not my specialty and considering the time and resources it could take I left it out of the original scope completely. 
But now that the game is officially out it might be the time to retake that idea and find a way to include some narrative or story into the game. Again I’m still planning on it so there is no date for this yet.

What I can say is that no matter what I’ll end up doing my goal is to finish everything before the 1 year anniversary of the game or even the 6 month anniversary. So all of this is for the long run. But as I said non of this might happen.

There are more surprises cooking in the back but more news on that when the time arrives.

Until then thanks again for the support on Hoping Forest and if you haven’t gotten it yet don’t miss the chance to enjoy this relaxing but challenging experience!

notes.title: General Update: Bug fixing and some quality-of-life improvements.
notes.notes:
🐸 - The first update of Hoping Forest is here! - 🐸

Thanks to everyone that buy the game and all the support during it first week.

Sadly the game launched with some bugs that didn’t show up in QA, some of these bugs prevented the correct progress of the game. They were all fixed in this update, but still, if you found any bug or issue in the game please let me know so I can fix it as soon as I can.

Bugs fixed:

 The progress didn't take into account correctly the scores of the levels in zone 2, preventing some achievements. This is fixed and the progress should update automatically as soon as you open the game giving the corresponding achievements.
 Cars could drift away from the streets. Sometimes the cars didn’t rotate as they should in the corners drifting away in the streets and breaking the levels, preventing their competition. Now the cars check their rotation and fix themselves if something went wrong.
 Tiles could end up with wrong rotations. Sometimes, especially if quick and fast movements were made, the tiles could end up with a wrong rotation preventing the competition of the puzzles. Now the tiles check their rotation and fix themselves if something went wrong.
 The Start Path button sometimes vanishes. Almost all the UI animations are made with an asset that helps with this kind of animation, but sometimes it failed with specific elements, apparently, the Start Path button was one of these elements. To prevent this the way that animation worked was changed completely to prevent this issue.
 Various small bugs fixed

However, there are some bugs I'm still working on, these are:

Known bugs:

 Sometimes the tiles can get stuck preventing any interaction with them, however, this only lasts a few seconds and fix itself after some time or while interacting with other tiles.

There are also some quality-of-life improvements that were added, these changes were left out initially in the previous version of the game due to deadlines, these are:

Quality-of-life improvements:

 Language selection is now stored. After the updating, you will still need to select the language when you launched the game, but going forward the game will load automatically to the main menu. To change the language you’ll need to do it in the options.
 Windowed mode added. Now you can toggle between fullscreen and window mode. The fullscreen is the default option and the recommended way of playing the game.
 Options in the pause menu inside the puzzles. Now you can access the options of the game in the pause menu during the puzzles with the exception of the language selection, this is still exclusive to the main menu. 


The demo version was also updated. Previously the demo was one update behind and didn’t have some details that are present in the full version of the game. Now both of them are in the same version.

There are also some small improvements to the demo:


  Now in the puzzle selection you can see the layout of the zones with the rest of the puzzles blocked. This should help to give a better picture of the whole content of the game for those who preferred trying it first instead of just showing an empty space.


I hope all these changes improve the overall experience of the game, if you find any other bug or issue within the game please let me know in the comments of this announcement or via email at contact@arthemystudios.com so I can fix it as soon as possible.

Thanks again for all the support and for those who hadn’t bought the game yet don’t miss the chance to play Hoping Forest now with the Steam Puzzle Fest discount.

notes.title: Hoping Forest has a release date! April 24,2023
notes.notes:
After many months of development, the official release date of Hoping Forest is finally confirmed.

April 24, 2023

It’s been months of hard work but the big day is close. With wholesome aesthetic and challenging puzzles, Hoping Forest offers a unique experience to those who love puzzle games.

Help the frog find a new home after seeing their forest destroyed by human progress and the waters invaded by dangerous creatures.

Find the hidden paths that lead to your goal and pick all the flies you can while avoiding the dangers within the forest. And most importantly, never lose hope.

Wishlist Hoping Forest to get the launch notification and don’t miss the opportunity to try the demo available now.
